summary: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport (OXB) is the principal international gateway to Guinea-Bissau, located just a few kilometers northwest of the capital city of Bissau. Named after the country's former head of state, it handles the vast majority of the nation's commercial air traffic and serves as a vital link for this small West African coastal nation. The airport features a single runway and modest terminal facilities typical of regional African hubs, supporting flights to neighboring countries and select European destinations.
faqs:
Q: What is the main international airport in Guinea-Bissau?
A: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport (OXB) in Bissau is the country's primary international airport, handling the bulk of commercial flights in and out of the nation.

Q: Are there direct flights from Europe to Osvaldo Vieira Airport?
A: Limited direct European service has historically connected Bissau with Lisbon and other European cities, though schedules and carriers vary. Most international travelers connect through other West African hubs.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Bissau?
A: The airport is located only a short drive from central Bissau, typically around 7-10 kilometers northwest of the city center.

Q: Does the airport operate 24 hours?
A: Operating hours are limited and tied to scheduled flight arrivals and departures, so travelers should confirm flight times in advance, especially for early morning or late evening flights.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared minibuses are the most common ways to reach the airport from Bissau city center, with journey times usually under 20 minutes depending on traffic. Travelers should agree on fares in advance, as metered taxis are not standard practice. Arranging hotel pickup or a pre-booked transfer is recommended for added convenience and security.
local_tip: Keep small denomination West African CFA francs on hand for taxi fares and small purchases, as change for larger bills is often difficult to find at and around the airport.
